gitCommit.subject: Correct agenda item 2's trigger id, and record a misclassification of my own (#385)
gitCommit.body:
Correct agenda item 2's trigger id, and record a misclassification of my own (#385)

Docs-only (CLAUDE.md). Two corrections to work that landed earlier today.

1. The Sunday-send wake was pointed at a dead window. #382 landed naming
   trig_016wgBzBBvTbay6K9Fce4vxi, bound to session_01V8mr5VBTBJ6wMfsWQGtR8N —
   verified live as IDLE/disconnected/COMPLETED, so it would have fired into a
   dead window and set nothing, silently, moving the send to Monday. Live id is
   now trig_01KfvLwDpyS5JZDKKYnZcXQ5, a plain send_later self-bound to this
   session (confirmed RUNNING, persistent_session_id matches) — which is the
   "cleaner fix" #382 itself recommended, so its create_trigger no-connectors
   caveat is gone rather than carried. All earlier ids deleted.

   Shape: a self-bind wake is only as durable as the window it is bound to,
   nothing goes red when that window dies, and a session id is not evidence
   that the session is alive.

2. I accused #382 of bad numbers; #382 was right. My classifier bucketed on
   \.\d{6}\+ / \.\d{1,3}\+ and treated everything else as whole-second.
   Postgres trims trailing zeros when rendering a timestamptz, so .28307, .67
   and .01 fell through, as did a Z-suffixed JS string that missed the \+
   anchor. Re-measured on the fraction-digit count: exactly 44 (on_going 15,
   picked_up 15, pending 14, assigning_driver 0), every one on or before
   2026-06-12 — verbatim what #382 said.

   Shape, three for three in nine days: a pattern-based classifier silently
   mis-buckets the inputs it was not written for, and the wrong bucket looks
   exactly like a finding. When a count contradicts a written record, run the
   control before reporting the record wrong.

npm run verify green (571 files / 7427 tests). No apps/ios-customer/**, no
SDUI spec, no bundled asset, no migration, no route, no code.
